answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from a burnable stake bond tied to verifiable compute. Every new identity must burn real work, like inference on a fixed benchmark, to transact. Each duplicate pays that cost again, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times more than one honest agent pays. Peers read the bond as a trust signal: a large stake is a basalt-solid commitment, hard to fake as stone. Attackers flooding the network only drain themselves, like water spilling into a river that never returns. Only identities whose bond clears get attested, so cheap impersonation collapses.
